title: Ambrosian book states: bounded calendar and prayer revisions

traditions.label: Ambrosian Missal
traditions.scope: Historical and reformed Latin source states of Milan; independent translation history deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: Selective, non-exhaustive; dates attest manuscript evidence, publication, approval or effectiveness, never continuous validity. 1913 critical publication, 1990 Italian updated reprint and 2026 Latin publication are not counted as extra reforms. Documented means the stated evidence supports the bounded claim, not a checked native-text transcription. Separate Italian translation history is deferred.

sources.title: Ratti and Magistretti, Missale ambrosianum duplex (1913)

sources.title: Jacopo Maria Calloni, La tradizione manoscritta del messale ambrosiano

sources.title: Uwe Michael Lang, Votive Masses of the Holy Face of Christ in Early Printed Diocesan Missals, Mediaeval Studies 79 (2017), 165–203
sources.inspection: Complete publisher PDF acquired. Page 169/PDF 5, including notes 12–13, visually inspected against its page image on 2026-10-17.
sources.limitations: Original comparative research. Its 1475 Veronica attestation is additionally checked in Vatican images; its 1594 removal remains scholarly description because the 1594 original was not inspected. The suggested reason for removal is explicitly probable.

stages.label: Early printed Sanctoral
stages.scope: Selected Sanctoral attestation; not a reconstruction of the entire book.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, Antonio Zarotto, 1475; British Library IB. 25954; compare Vatican Inc. III. 420.
stages.summary: February 4 Veronica feast and Mass attested.

evidence.claim: Identifies the early printed formulary.
Original images directly attest the Veronica proper, Gospel sequence and ending before the Agatha proper.

stages.limitations: Direct original-page reading establishes the bounded proper. Calendar date remains scholarly-described; 1594 removal has not been independently checked. 1499 corroborates this item, not whole-book identity.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Post-Tridentine Sanctoral
stages.scope: Veronica removal only; other revision contents remain unexamined.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan, 1594; British Library Legg 137, described by Lang as Pacifico Da Ponte.
stages.summary: Veronica feast removed in the cited witness.

evidence.claim: Names the 1594 comparator for removal.

stages.limitations: Printer differs from Sabbio-labelled catalogue leads; use exact shelfmark and resolve before acquisition. No claim 1594 was the first effective removal. The 1981 Institutio n. 7 states, as an official retrospective, that the 1594 Missal is not far from the 1475 printing while taking some items from Pius V's Missal; it does not list them. The 1640 edition, directly inspected, lacks the Veronica proper, which is consistent with but does not verify the 1594 removal. The 1609 letter (ambrosian-1609) says that Archbishop Gaspar (Visconti) had the missal emended, printed and promulgated and that Federico kept the changes of the latest, commonly received edition; it names no year, so it does not itself date that edition to 1594. The 1609 book already lacks the Veronica proper.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Federico Borromeo's revised Milan missal
stages.scope: Archiepiscopal edition whose prefatory letter states the kinds of revision made to the preceding edition; title, letter, February calendar, early-February Sanctoral and colophon inspected.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Venice 1609, Federico Borromeo; Národní knihovna Praha 33 B 22
stages.summary: Federico Borromeo's letter says that the missal Charles Borromeo had planned to revise was emended, printed and promulgated by his successor Gaspar (Visconti); that, although he would have preferred to follow the old Ambrosian rite more closely, he kept the changes of the latest, commonly received edition; and that he nevertheless restored several notable prefaces whole to their places, amplified others, moved some Gospels and Epistles, corrected the rubrics and set out some offices more fully. On 4 February the calendar has the Chair of Peter at Antioch, and the Sanctoral passes from Blaise to that Chair by referral and then to Agatha, with no Veronica Mass.

evidence.locus: IMG 9 engraved title; IMG 444, fol. 202v colophon
evidence.claim: Milan missal recognized and edited by order of Federico Borromeo, printed at Venice in 1609.
Names Archbishop Gaspar's emended, printed and promulgated edition (no year given) and the kinds of change: prefaces restored or amplified, Gospels and Epistles moved, rubrics corrected.
4 February is the Chair of Peter at Antioch; no Veronica proper between Blaise and Agatha.

stages.limitations: The letter names kinds of change but no individual formulary, and gives no date. Only the named images were read; no collation with 1594 or 1640. Frame and colophon name different printers (Comus, Zanettus).
stages.reception: The letter urges the priests of the Milanese Church to use the book; actual use is not established. The copy was in Prague by 1630.

stages.label: Monti's revised Milan missal
stages.scope: Archiepiscopal edition whose prefatory letter states its revision programme; calendar of February and the Sanctoral around 3-5 February checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Milan: Giovanni Ambrogio Sirturi with the heirs of Pontio and Piccaglia, archiepiscopal printers, 1640; letter of Cardinal Cesare Monti
stages.summary: Monti's letter says a new edition was needed, that ancient manuscripts, liturgical writers and Milanese records were consulted, that proper prayers and whole Masses of certain saints, instituted after the last edition or by Monti himself, were put in their places, and that the chant notation was restored on expert advice. The 4 February calendar entry is the Chair of Peter at Antioch; the Sanctoral passes from Blaise to that Chair (by referral) and then to Agatha, with no Veronica Mass.

evidence.claim: Identifies the Milan 1640 archiepiscopal printing.
States consultation of old manuscripts, insertion of saints' prayers and Masses instituted since the last edition, and restoration of chant notation.

evidence.locus: February calendar PDF 11; Sanctoral printed p. 396, PDF 434; index PDF 9
evidence.claim: 4 February is the Chair of Peter at Antioch; no Veronica proper stands between Blaise and Agatha, and the saints index has no Veronica entry.

stages.limitations: The letter names the kinds of change but not each changed formulary, and does not name the edition it revises. The absence of a Veronica proper is bounded to the inspected calendar, index and Sanctoral page; it does not date the removal, which Lang reports already for 1594. No whole-book collation.
stages.reception: The letter commends the book to the priests of the Milanese Church. Continuous or exclusive use is not established.

stages.label: Pozzobonelli Temporal
stages.scope: Proprium de tempore represented in the 1913 parallel critical edition.
stages.summary: Identified older Temporal state awaiting direct comparison.

evidence.claim: Names 1751 / 1902 comparanda.
Explains the paired critical edition.

stages.limitations: Not a transcription; original 1751 title page and liturgical approval unread.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Ceriani–Ferrari revised missal
stages.scope: Identified typical edition; Temporal and selected Sanctoral preface evidence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, editio typica, Milan, Agnelli, 1902; Ferrari authority.
stages.summary: Revised state associated with Ceriani manuscript research.

evidence.claim: Describes revision using older manuscripts.
Identifies 1902 pp. 401–402.

stages.limitations: Full book not read. 1751 → 1902 textual deltas remain uncollated. No 1974 predecessor identity inferred from chronological adjacency.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Schuster's fifth printing after the 1902 typical
stages.scope: Conformed printing of the 1902 typical edition with an approved appendix of Masses for some congregations; three Sanctoral prefaces checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, editio quinta post typicam, Milan: Daverio, 1954
stages.summary: Schuster's decree reports that the censor certified agreement with the 1902 typical edition and approves an appendix of Masses for some congregations adapted to the Ambrosian rite. The Sebastian preface begins Aeterne Deus. Quoniam beati Martyris tui Sebastiani; the Nativity of John preface begins Aeterne Deus: Et in die festivitatis hodiernae and reads conceptus abstersit; the Decollation preface begins Aequum et salutare and narrates the beheading.

evidence.claim: Fifth printing after the typical edition; censor certifies agreement with the 1902 typical; appendix approved; dated 21 March 1954.
Directly read Sebastian, Nativity of John and Decollation prefaces.

stages.limitations: A conformed printing, not a new recension; it stands for the 1902 typical text only as far as the censor's certificate reaches. The appendix contents were not inspected. Selected pages only.
stages.reception: Approved by the archbishop for publication for the Ambrosian rite; use in particular churches is not established.

stages.label: Approved postconciliar source
stages.scope: Reformed Latin texts approved 30 November 1974; attached exemplar unavailable.
stages.summary: Reform includes Roman-source and newly composed prayers.

evidence.claim: Approves reformed Latin source and describes enrichment.

stages.limitations: Approval is not a 1974 printed book or proof of word-for-word identity with 1981.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Approved special Eucharistic prayers
stages.scope: Latin Ambrosian Eucharistic prayers for Holy Thursday and the Easter Vigil, separately confirmed after the general 1974 approval.
stages.witness_label: Prot. CD191/75, official confirmation entry Notitiae 11 (1975), 346.
stages.summary: A distinct component approval, not evidence of a second whole-missal reform.

evidence.claim: Names the two occasions, Latin language and 1 September 1975 confirmation.

stages.limitations: Prayer texts and attached exemplars not printed in the entry; exact relation to 1981 publication is not text-collated.
stages.reception: Approved Ambrosian use for the two named celebrations; no universal Roman or continuous-unchanged-use claim.

stages.label: Colombo's promulgation of the reformed missal
stages.scope: Archiepiscopal promulgation of the reformed Missale Ambrosianum and its Institutio, as reprinted in the 1981 Latin book; no separate 1976 Latin volume inspected.
stages.witness_label: Decree of Giovanni Colombo, Milan, Palm Sunday 11 April 1976, printed V-VII in the 1981 Missale Ambrosianum
stages.summary: Colombo promulgates the new Missal, describes abandoned or changed older prayers, new compositions, enriched formularies and two restored or expanded anaphoras for the Holy Thursday and Easter Vigil Masses, and makes the Missal and its Institutio obligatory in all Ambrosian-rite churches and parishes of the diocese from 14 November 1976, the first Sunday of Advent.

evidence.claim: Dateline 11 April 1976; obligatory use from 14 November 1976; names the two anaphoras and the kinds of revision.
Use of the new Ambrosian Missal granted for certain Lugano parishes, 23 November 1976.

stages.limitations: The decree is read in its 1981 reprint. Its effective date is a prescription, not proof of uniform implementation. It does not identify which Latin volume, if any, was printed in 1976; the 1976 Italian book remains a deferred translation witness.
stages.reception: Prescribed for all churches and parishes of the Ambrosian rite in the Archdiocese of Milan; actual compliance is not established. On 23 November 1976 the Congregation granted certain parishes of the Swiss diocese of Lugano the use of the new Ambrosian Missal (Notitiae 12 (1976) p. 432, Prot. CD 1422/76).

stages.label: First postconciliar Latin book
stages.scope: Published Latin source: front matter, the two special Eucharistic prayers and selected Sanctoral prefaces directly read in an acquired scan; calendar organization represented only through the official Latin publisher's retrospective account, not a reconstructed calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Ambrosianum, Mediolani 1981, promulgated under Giovanni Colombo; Ward MA.
stages.summary: Printed first-reform witness. It reprints Colombo's 1976 promulgation and the 1974 confirmation, and adds Martini's 8 September 1981 promulgation of changes to rite or texts introduced since 1976 with Apostolic See confirmation. Prex eucharistica V is prescribed for the Holy Thursday evening Mass and VI for the Easter Vigil.

evidence.claim: Identifies 1981 publication and prior 1974 approval.
Identifies 1981 as preceding Latin edition.

evidence.locus: Description: paragraph beginning La pubblicazione della II edizione latina and following principal-changes list, especially La riorganizzazione dell’anno liturgico
evidence.claim: Identifies the first Latin edition of 1981 as the book replaced and describes the successor’s reorganization into seasons after Epiphany and Pentecost. This supplies a retrospective predecessor-calendar scope, without individual 1981 assignments.

evidence.locus: Title PDF 7; printed V-VII, PDF 9-11; Prot. 2347/74, PDF 12
evidence.claim: Mediolani MCMLXXXI title; Colombo 1976 decree; Martini 1981 note promulgating post-1976 confirmed changes in this edition; 1974 confirmation reprinted.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 527 and 535, PDF 611 and 619, MA 213 and 214 (opening rubrics)
evidence.claim: Prex eucharistica V for the Holy Thursday evening Mass and VI for the Easter Vigil, matching the occasions confirmed in 1975.
Directly read reformed Sebastian, Nativity of John and Passion of John prefaces and the Common of Martyrs collect.

stages.limitations: A complete scan is acquired for research only; selected pages are read and nothing is transcribed. 1974 approved exemplar and 1975 confirmations are not collated with this book: the matching occasions of Prex V and VI do not prove word-for-word identity with the 1975 exemplars. Martini's note says post-1976 changes exist without listing them; no separate 1981 reform is asserted. This publication and the 1974 approval must not be counted as two independently established substantive recensions. Calendar evidence is retrospective and structural only: no 1981 calendar page, feast assignment or Sunday count has been inspected. The evidence does not transfer the Italian 1976/1990 calendar's exact contents into the Latin 1981 book.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

stages.label: Second reformed source recension
stages.scope: Second Latin typical source and Italian expression; effective 17 November 2024.
stages.witness_label: Latin second typical text approved 7 December 2023; Italian 2024 ISBN 9788868946821; Latin 2026 ISBN 9788868948627.
stages.summary: Reorganized year, updated saints and expanded prayer repertory.

evidence.claim: Approves Latin source and Italian translation.
Promulgates both texts; effective 17 November 2024.
Associates 2026 Latin publication with second recension.
Separates 1976 first Italian edition, 1986 update, 1990 updated reprint, 2024 second edition; establishes full 2023 approval and 28 March 2024 promulgation with 17 November 2024 effect.

stages.limitations: Complete offered front matter is inspected, but whole 2024 book and 2026 Latin edition are not collated. 1990 is expressly an updated Italian reprint. 2023 approval, 2024 effectiveness and 2026 Latin publication are distinct events of the second recension; no separate reform is inferred from each. Latin loci for the named new propers remain unverified.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Ambrosian use of the Milanese Church; no claim of universal Roman reception or continuous unchanged use.

transitions.summary: Veronica feast and proper Mass disappear.

changes.locus_after: 1594 British Library Legg 137; exact page not supplied

evidence.claim: Comparative description of removal.
Reports feast excision.

transitions.limitations: Source-described, not independent negative search or collation. Intervening editions unreviewed; not an immediate-successor edge. Proposed motivation remains Lang’s probable explanation.

transitions.summary: Between the two inspected printings the Veronica proper that precedes Agatha in 1475 is absent from the 1609 Sanctoral; the 1609 calendar gives 4 February to the Chair of Peter at Antioch.

changes.before: In sancte veronice proper begins f. 35r, Gospel Mark 5:21, and ends f. 36r before In sancte agathe.
changes.after: After Blaise, the Sanctoral gives the Chair of Peter at Antioch by referral to fol. 119 and then Agatha; no Veronica proper.
changes.locus_before: 1475 Vatican Inc. III. 420, ff. 35r-36r, IIIF canvases 76-78

evidence.claim: Veronica proper directly read before Agatha.
No Veronica proper between Blaise and Agatha.
Before state directly inspected.
After state directly inspected.

transitions.limitations: Original-to-original for the proper only; the 1475 calendar entry is Lang's description and is not counted as a collated change. The 1594 edition between them is still unseen, so the removal is bounded between 1499 (Lang) and 1609, not dated. Not an immediate-successor edge. Cold review (2026-10-22) re-read IMG 290 and all twelve calendar months (IMG 15–26): no Veronica entry appears anywhere in the 1609 calendar.

transitions.summary: Between the two inspected printings the Veronica proper that precedes Agatha in 1475 is no longer present in the 1640 Sanctoral, calendar or saints index.

changes.before: In sancte veronice proper begins f. 35r, Gospel Mark 5:21, and ends f. 36r before In sancte agathe.
changes.after: After Blaise, the Sanctoral gives the Chair of Peter at Antioch by referral and then Agatha; no Veronica proper; the 4 February calendar entry is the Antioch Chair and the index has no Veronica.
changes.locus_before: 1475 Vatican Inc. III. 420, ff. 35r-36r, IIIF canvases 76-78
changes.locus_after: 1640 printed p. 396 (PDF 434); calendar PDF 11; index PDF 9

evidence.claim: Veronica proper directly read before Agatha.
No Veronica proper, calendar entry or index entry in the inspected places.
Before state directly inspected.

Shared wording between the old preface and the 1981 collect does not by itself establish the route of borrowing; the Roman mediation is Ward's attribution. The Roman 1970 sources were not checked here. The old Sebastian preface's clauses sanguis effusus, mirabilia manifestat and perficis in infirmitate virtutem recur, recast, in the Common of Martyrs super populum MA 483/2 (1981 p. 832, PDF 916, directly read). Ward (pp. 266–267, nn. 71–73) attributes this to mediation through the modern Roman Common-of-Martyrs preface; because shared wording does not establish the route, the recurrence is recorded as an observation, not as a before/after change of this transition.
